Jana: Pushing a short perf dump from last night's adaptive-batcher + kernel selector run. Noticing increased tail token latency for the /long-docs route. attaching quick numbers and GPU snapshot.
Perf Bot: Automated snapshot uploaded: https://dash.redwood.internal/snapshots/1912345678 (contains per-route token breakdown + GPU telemetry) :satellite:
Mike: Saw the snapshot, thanks. Can you paste the p50/p95/p99 token latencies here?
Jana: Pls see snippet below (sampled 1k requests, windows=50ms):
```
route: /short -> p50=12ms p95=28ms p99=65ms
route: /chat -> p50=14ms p95=40ms p99=120ms
route: /long-docs -> p50=35ms p95=210ms p99=520ms
avg_tokens_per_req: short=48 chat=92 long-docs=420
```
Priya: ugh p99 520ms for long-docs is rough. Any KV cache insights? hit/miss rate?
Jana: KV cache global hit-rate looks fine overall (~92%) but route-level shows long-docs has a higher priming miss spike. snippet:
```
route,long_kv_miss,kv_hits
/long-docs,0.16,0.84
/chat,0.03,0.97
/short,0.01,0.99
```
Ryan: Could be kernel selector thrash + batching window interplay. I noticed the kernel selector flapping between fused-attn-v2 and baseline when seq_len>2k which causes an extra kernel swap + memcpy that hurts tail. SM occupancy drops during swaps.
Jana: GPU telemetry around the p99 tail window:
```
SM_occupancy: avg=82% tail=45%
VRAM_used: avg=11.2GB tail=12.9GB (24GB card)
GPU_power: avg=210W tail=275W
GPU_temp: avg=68C tail=82C
MIG_slices_active: 2/4 with imbalance on slice-1
kernel_switch_count: 18 spikes during tail windows
```
Mike: That kernel_switch_count is telling. When selector flips we likely drop from the fast fused kernels back to a safer kernel that doesn't support our quant path -> memcpy+repack. Suggest trying kernel_pin for the fused kernel for the long-docs route to see if it stabilizes tail.
Priya: Also worth checking KV cache staleness: if priming leads to repeated cache warms we add many small requests that don't batch well. Can we measure "priming_tokens_per_session"?
Jana: I extracted priming tokens metric: long-docs priming_tokens_per_session ~ 320 vs chat ~ 40. That amplifies the batching inefficiency.
Ryan: Proposed quick experiments:
- A: kernel_pin fused-attn-v2 on long-docs (50% traffic)
- B: increase adaptive-batcher window from 50ms -> 120ms for long-docs
- C: enable prefix-caching TTL=30m to reduce repeated priming

Config snippets:
```yaml
routes:
  - name: long-docs
    match: "/long-docs"
    kernel_override: fused-attn-v2
    batcher:
      adaptive_window_ms: 120
      max_batch_size: 16
cache:
  prefix_ttl: 1800  # seconds
```
Mike: If we A/B those we should instrument per-route kernel_switch_count, per-route p99 token latency, kv_priming_tokens, and SM occupancy by slice. Add dashboards and an alert: p99_token_latency(route)/ > 300ms for 5m -> page oncall.
Priya: I'll add the dashboard panels and a lightweight eval that runs a 10-request long-docs synthetic trace to validate tail.
Jana: After running a quick local sim with kernel_pin + window=120ms i see p99 drop from 520ms -> ~220ms in the sim. SM occupancy stabilizes ~78% with fewer dips. Need cluster run for realtime numbers.
Perf Bot: Scheduled canary perf run at 1912349200 for config set: kernel_pin+window120+prefix_ttl1800. Results will auto-upload. :gear:
Mike: Nice. Also add a histogram panel for token-level service_time broken down by batch_size and kernel_name. That helped us catch similar issues before.
Ryan: FYI add a tiny metric: kernel_selector_latency_ms — if selector decision takes >5ms we should log sample of stack.
Priya: Putting todos in a short checklist in the ticket: 1) dashboard panels 2) canary run 3) A/B configs 4) alert 5) postmortem if >2x regressions.
Jana: Thanks all. I'll kick off the canary and post results in this thread. :eyes:
Mike: :thumbsup:
Perf Bot: Canary created -> run_id=canary-1912349200-01. Uploading telemetry to https://dash.redwood.internal/canaries/canary-1912349200-01
Jana: closing the loop once we have the canary numbers.
